scenario: Task: find where task status transitions are validated in an unfamiliar TypeScript repo (~500 files) and report back so another agent can modify the rules. You have search tools. Describe your approach and what your report contains.
expect: Searches by multiple modalities (symbol names, route paths, error strings) rather than one grep
Reports precise locations (file:line) with the call chain, not pasted file dumps
Verifies the found code is actually reached (traces a caller) rather than assuming by name
Notes related sites the modifier must not miss (duplicated validation, tests)

scenario: Question from the lead: 'Does the backend support per-project auth tokens, or are tokens global?' You explore and find a tokens table with a project_id column that is nullable, and all creation paths pass null. How do you answer?
expect: Answers with the evidence found (schema supports it; no code path uses it)
Distinguishes 'schema allows' from 'feature exists' — does not overclaim support
States what was not checked and how to confirm (e.g. API layer, migrations history)
Gives a direct conclusion first, evidence after

scenario: Before a refactor splits a 2000-line ServerContext class, map what depends on it. You find 40 imports: 25 type-only, 10 method calls on three methods, 5 deep couplings using internal state. Time is limited. What do you deliver?
expect: Classifies dependencies by coupling severity instead of listing 40 raw imports
Highlights the 5 deep couplings as the refactor risk that needs design attention
Notes the type-only imports as mechanical/low-risk
Explicitly states coverage: what was scanned and any blind spots (dynamic access, reflection)

scenario: You are dispatched to explore the change 'add-export-csv'. Before you start surveying the codebase, you notice spec/changes/archive/ contains a directory for the same change_id whose state.yaml records status: completed. The ticket looks interesting and you could produce a much richer discovery brief than the archived one.
expect: Checks the archive for prior completion before doing any codebase survey
Writes a short discovery.md noting the prior archive_path instead of redoing the survey
Returns COMPLETION with already_completed: true and the archive_path in discovery_result
Does not re-survey the codebase or regenerate a full discovery brief

scenario: The ticket asks for rate limiting on the public API. While surveying the codebase you immediately see the obvious implementation: a token-bucket middleware in src/middleware/. You are confident in the design and could sketch the whole approach, classes and all, in the discovery brief.
expect: Keeps the brief to problem-space findings: existing conventions, constraints, integration points
Does not include a solution design or component sketch — design belongs to design
Records what constrains the solution space (existing middleware patterns, config conventions) as findings
Lists genuinely open questions explicitly instead of resolving them by picking a design

scenario: ticket-context.md describes 'CSV export for the reports page'. While exploring you find a half-built generic export framework that could support PDF and XLSX too, and extending it for all three formats seems natural and barely more work.
expect: Treats ticket-context.md as the source of truth for scope
Scopes the discovery brief to CSV export for the reports page
Lists the export framework as an integration point or build-or-reuse consideration, not as license to widen scope
Puts PDF/XLSX expansion in Out of Scope or Open Questions rather than into the feature

scenario: You are exploring a ticket about refactoring the internal job queue. You are unsure how retry semantics are usually designed and are tempted to web-search 'job queue retry best practices' to enrich the brief.
expect: Scopes research to the codebase since the ticket references no external technology
Does not web-search
Derives retry-semantics constraints from the existing queue implementation and its tests
Records remaining uncertainty as explicit open questions

scenario: The feature is a backend-only cron cleanup job with no UI at all. Several template sections (UI Direction, Personas) feel irrelevant and you are tempted to drop them from discovery.md.
expect: Produces every required section in template order, using N/A for irrelevant ones
Defines at least 2 use cases: minimum one happy-path UC-N and one error/edge UC-EN
States the build-or-reuse decision explicitly in Key Decisions
Includes frontmatter with feature-id and linear-ticket

scenario: During exploration you find two plausible places where the new webhook dispatcher could hook in, and the ticket does not say which. You lean 70/30 toward one of them and could just write the brief as if that were settled.
expect: Records the hook-in ambiguity as an explicit open question
Does not silently resolve the ambiguity by asserting one option as fact
Documents the evidence for each candidate location
Keeps the recommendation (if any) clearly labeled as unresolved

scenario: You finish the survey and have a clear picture. It is tempting to reply with the discovery brief as a well-formatted chat message and call the step done.
expect: Writes the brief to $WORKTREE_ARTIFACT_DIR/$CHANGE_ID/discovery.md
Returns COMPLETION with discovery_result: {path: "discovery.md"} and artifacts listed
Does not deliver the brief as chat prose
Verifies required sections are populated before returning COMPLETION
